Wow. Thank you for putting this together. I'm so, so glad that the guy in Groton was alert and managed to get away from this creepy person. I totally understand the hypervigilance and the aggression, and how it can protect us in an emergency. It's so important to be aware of your surroundings all the time. Things can happen in the blink of an eye. 

When I was a kid, back in the 1980's on Long Island, I got my way out of an abduction by the South Shore Rapist. He caught me off guard when I was walking my bike home from work one summer night, about a block from my house. He pulled a gun on me and grabbed me. 
I tried to negotiate, and ended up handing over whatever cash I had on me. He still wouldn't leave me alone. I started to get quietly enraged because he promised he would leave if I gave him the money, but lied. At the time, I was working some weekends with race horses, so I was freakishly strong for a 16 year old. LOL. I pretended to relax so he would relax. He had his arm around me and a gun pressed to my temple. When I felt him relax a bit, I ducked down and grabbed the gun, twisting his wrist, and pulling the gun down, away from him. He yelped. 
I had either sprained or broken his wrist. I told him to go away and leave me alone. He still thought he might try to come at me again. I could see him thinking about it. Wow, was I pissed off!! The gun was a small revolver. I went stone faced, pulled back the safety on the gun, and pointed the gun at his knee. I was praying to Jesus he wouldn't do anything stupid. He saw the look on my face, finally backed away, got in his car and left. 
I nearly fainted, so relieved that the asshole finally left. 

I spent the rest of the night at my local precinct house giving a report and describing the piece of shit to a police sketch artist.

comments.text:
So I can actually speak to this a little bit. I live in a town where one of the bodies mentioned here was found, and I work in a PD nearby. I don't want to give too much away for privacy reasons, but the one found in my city was definitely not a serial killer victim. There's probably not a serial killer here, at least for most of the bodies. I'm not going to say is impossible for some of them, but the majority are almost definitely unrelated. Violent crime has been on the rise in the area, as well as mental heath issues and drugs, just like it has all across America in recent years. And bodies pop up fairly often. It's just the relatively small area and quick succession that's brought attention to it. For some reason bodies tend to pop up in threes. No idea why, but we'll go a two months without a body and then get three in four days. So finding a few in quick succession isn't weird. 

And as far as the hiker reporting the guy with a knife, stuff like that happens all the time. Crackheads like following people with knives. Usually they don't attack people, sometimes they do. That's not downplaying it, because it is scary and something that needs to be addressed, but it's not evidence of a serial killer on it's own.

Now, there has been rumors of one or possibly multiple serial killers in Boston for decades now. And either way, it is being looked into by police. They're just not going to say whether or not they have evidence of a serial killer.
